newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says all troops withdrawn from Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Russia says all troops withdrawn from Chechnya.

text.p: Russia has withdrawn the last of its defence ministry troops from Chechnya, a ministry spokesman said on Sunday.

"Today there are no defence ministry troops in Chechnya. They are all withdrawn," said defence ministry spokesman Viktor Tkachenko. The withdrawal of all interior ministry troops from the rebel region had been announced earlier on Sunday.
A different defence ministry official had said earlier on Sunday that some troops remained in the region.
Tkachenko said he did not know exactly when the last troops had been pulled out but that they had left before the departure of the last interior ministry troops.

President Boris Yeltsin sent the troops to the region in December 1994, starting a bloody and ill-fated 21-month military campaign against separatists. He ordered the gradual withdrawal to pave the way for elections on January 27.
The pullout marks a formal end to the conflict, which killed tens of thousands of people, mostly civilians, before a ceasefire and peace deal was signed in August.
